findings.why: The site has an address on the internet.
The domain explicitly says it never receives email. Spoofing protection below still matters for SENDING.
Receivers are told to reject mail from unlisted servers.
An empty key tells receivers this domain does not sign mail. Correct for a domain that sends no email; a problem if it does.
Spoofed mail is thrown away. Strongest setting.
Without a report address you never learn who is spoofing you.

findings.result: plain http serves the full site
findings.why: The unencrypted version works. On public wifi, anyone nearby can read what visitors send - including login cookies.
A visitor's first request can be downgraded to http by an attacker on the same network.
Another site can load this one in an invisible frame and hijack clicks.
Browsers may execute a file as script even when it is not meant to be.
No allow-list for scripts. Any injected script runs. Common gap, worth fixing on sites that take payments or logins.
Minor. Other sites can see the full URL a visitor came from.
Attackers are not told which software or version is running.

findings.result: behind Cloudflare - origin server is hidden
findings.why: Good: attackers cannot reach the server directly either. Ports on this IP belong to Cloudflare's network, not to this site.
Config, backup and source-control files are not downloadable.
No obvious admin door on the front of the site.
